raw_segments.text: If direct taxes upon the wages of labor have not always occasioned a proportionable rise
in those wages, it is because they have generally occasioned a considerable fall in the demand
The declension of industry, the decrease of employment for the poor, the diminution of
the annual produce of the land and labor of the country have generally been the effects
In consequence of them, however, the price of labor must always be higher than it otherwise
would have been in the actual state of the demand.
And this enhancement of price, together with the profit of those who advance it, must always
be finally paid by the landlords and consumers.
